verdict.rationale: uv records exact dependency versions in a cross-platform `uv.lock` and accepts version constraints in `uv add`. Its `--upgrade-package` flag upgrades only the named package and keeps the rest of the lockfile intact. Tools can be pinned with `{package}@{version}` (e.g. `uvx ruff@0.6.0`, `uv tool install`), tool upgrades respect install constraints, and `uv python pin` writes `.python-version`, which CI honors. The community report of a stale wheel version being sought is a lock-refresh annoyance, not a concrete failure of pinning. Missing for 10: tool pins are shown at global/invocation level rather than as project-scoped tool pins; no documented strict lockfile enforcement mode (e.g. failing installs that drift from the lock); only one thin independent confirmation that pins are respected in practice.
